solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cat draped round leg having sulk

indicators.note: something draped round another thing encloses it, so the cat's letters wrap the leg's

parts.note: mog is informal British slang for a cat
pin is informal for a leg, as in 'unsteady on your pins'

explanation.surface: A cat curled round someone's leg while they sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: To mope is to sulk listlessly, so someone having a sulk is in the act of doing just that.

clue.text: Senior politician wants skirt on rump made shorter

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt

indicators.note: making the word shorter means cutting its final letter off

parts.note: the stern is the rear end, of a ship or jokingly of a person

explanation.surface: A senior politician who fancies a short skirt over a slimmed-down behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A government minister heads a department, a senior figure in politics.

clue.text: Greek character on spacecraft to flirt

indicators.note: in a down clue, the Greek letter sits on top of the spacecraft

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a lander is a craft that sets down on a planet or moon

explanation.surface: A Greek man aboard a spaceship decides to flirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' looks like a person from Greece; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to flirt or have casual affairs, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: One regulated little sister's intellectual activity

indicators.note: regulated means brought into order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: sis is a short form of sister; the apostrophe-s stands for 'is' and links to the definition

explanation.surface: A well-behaved little sister engages in some thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Noesis is the philosophical term for cognition, the working of the intellect.

clue.text: Good bread in fact stale

indicators.note: the good bread sits inside the fact

parts.note: a stat, short for statistic, is a fact or figure
naan or nan is Indian flatbread

explanation.surface: A claim that good bread is actually stale.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water or air is stale from lack of movement; the sense extends to anything gone flat.

clue.text: Ballet article by head cryptographist?

parts.note: the definite article
nut is slang for the head
a code-cracker breaks ciphers

explanation.surface: A ballet piece written alongside a leading code expert.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the pun: a code-breaker cracks ciphers, so is a cracker.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's Christmas ballet is one of the best-known in the repertoire.

clue.text: Willing learner with an Asian ensemble

parts.note: game means willing, as in 'game for anything'
L is for learner, from British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: An eager pupil joins an Asian music group.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamelan is the traditional percussion orchestra of Java and Bali in Indonesia.

clue.text: An Italian city offers subtle charm

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, here written A
Roma is the Italian name for Rome

explanation.surface: An Italian city has a quiet, understated appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively an aroma is a pervasive quality or atmosphere, a subtle air of something.

clue.text: Computer enthusiast over time liable to blow fuse

indicators.note: the computer fan is over the time letter, covering it on both sides

parts.note: a techie or techy is someone keen on technology

explanation.surface: A computer fan who has worked too long is ready to blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tetchy is irritable, quick to lose their temper.

clue.text: Innocent one in place for congregation

indicators.note: the numeral sits inside the church area

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church where worshippers sit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An innocent person sitting among the churchgoers.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means lacking worldly experience, guileless and unsuspecting.

clue.text: Spoilt or bad meat in hunk

indicators.note: spoilt means ruined or messed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rotten meat found in a chunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hunk' reads as a lump of meat; it means an attractive man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal terms for a strikingly attractive man.

clue.text: Mann's novella — I've enhanced it spectacularly!

indicators.note: spectacularly here suggests the letters dramatically rearranged

explanation.surface: A boast about improving Thomas Mann's novella.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Mann published this novella in 1912, about Aschenbach's obsession with a boy in a plague-ridden city.

clue.text: Resilience enlivens non- European in recession

indicators.note: receding means moving backwards, so the remaining letters are read in reverse
non- tells us the European letter is not there

parts.note: to animate is to enliven or bring to life

explanation.surface: Economic resilience pepping up a country outside Europe during a downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-' removes E from ANIMATES, leaving ANIMATS; 'in recession' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the endurance to keep going.

clue.text: Not caught, Sam for example remains free

indicators.note: not here means without, so the caught letter is left out

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States, so Sam is an example of an uncle
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Sam escapes capture while the rest go free.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Sam is the figure personifying the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash is to let loose or set free, as with a dog off its lead.

clue.text: Heroic work companion right leaving cheesy town

indicators.note: the companion and right letters leave the town's name

parts.note: Cheddar is the Somerset village that gave its name to the cheese
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A heroic companion walks out of a cheese-making town.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEDDAR is a village in Somerset, England, famous for its cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is the medieval Icelandic collection of Norse mythological and heroic poems.

clue.text: Almost done with tea dance

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: done means cheated or swindled, as does conned

explanation.surface: Nearly finished, so time for tea and a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done' looks like finished; here it means swindled.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaconne is a stately Baroque dance built on a repeating bass line.

clue.text: Cleaner is coming in Tuesday having elevated service

indicators.note: the cleaner and is come into the middle of the day's letters
in a down clue, raising a word means reading it upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a British cleaning lady

explanation.surface: The cleaner turns up on Tuesday for a high church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having elevated' reverses TUE to EUT. 'Elevated service' suggests high church, but 'elevated' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eucharist is the Christian service of Holy Communion.

clue.text: Eccentric American avoiding press and public

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddball American who shuns the media and the crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal hearing held in private, closed to reporters and the public, takes place in camera.

clue.text: National obsession little man embodies

indicators.note: embodies means contains, so the man's name holds the obsession

parts.note: Ron is a short form of a man's name such as Ronald
a mania is an obsession

explanation.surface: A national fixation captured in one small fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Romania is a national of that country, the noun sense of national.

clue.text: Ropy work from staff packaging butter

indicators.note: packaging means wrapping round, so the staff encloses the butter

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff
a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter

explanation.surface: Staff wrapping up butter and doing a poor job of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is the dairy spread on the surface, but here it is something that butts, a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Macramé is decorative knotted craftwork made from cord or rope.

clue.text: Look quickly in small container

parts.note: a can is a metal container

explanation.surface: Glance inside a small tin.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan can mean to glance over quickly, skimming rather than studying.

clue.text: Strange craving observed in city up at top

indicators.note: the craving is seen inside the city
in a down clue, up means the city's letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
pica is an abnormal craving to eat non-food things like chalk or soil

explanation.surface: An odd hunger spotted in a city's upper reaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LA to AL. 'Strange' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the definition of pica.
explanation.definitionFit: Apical describes something at the apex or tip, so situated at the top.

clue.text: Old port — the writer's joining British sailors in it

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the letters for it

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is crossword shorthand for it

indicators.note: joining means placed next to, linking the possessive with the sailors

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, so the writer's is my
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: The author signs on with the Royal Navy and sails to an old harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Smyrna was the ancient Aegean seaport now known as Izmir in Turkey.

clue.text: Upright character escaping pain and hunger in style

indicators.note: the upright letter escapes, leaving the pain word

parts.note: the letter I stands straight up, a single vertical stroke
to ache is to hunger or yearn

explanation.surface: An upstanding person rising above pain and hunger with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright character' looks like a moral person; it is the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence, a flair or dash in one's manner.

clue.text: Renegade finally accepted by respectable relative

indicators.note: the letter is taken in by the respectable word

parts.note: nice in its sense of proper or respectable

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word renegade

explanation.surface: A rebel is at last welcomed by a respectable family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a member of the family.

clue.text: American friend in Soul City

indicators.note: the American friend sits inside the soul

parts.note: in ancient Egyptian belief the ka is the spiritual double or soul
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: An American buddy living in a city known for soul music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soul City' reads as one name; Soul is the Egyptian KA and City alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kampala is the capital city of Uganda.

clue.text: Sound cut in shout to encourage knight

indicators.note: the trimmed word sits inside the shout

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of encouragement

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: a sound argument is a valid one

explanation.surface: A noise cut into a cry of support for a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like noise; it means valid.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevalier is a French title for a knight or member of an order of chivalry.

clue.text: River sources only running high in northeast

indicators.note: only the sources, meaning the opening letters, of these words are used

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for northeast

explanation.surface: A river runs high only near its sources in the northeast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a major European river flowing from the Swiss Alps to the North Sea.

clue.text: Vassals convey false impression with info about me

parts.note: to lie is to convey a false impression

indicators.note: the information goes round, so it is about the word me

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Servants misrepresent things, mixing in some facts about the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Liegemen were feudal subjects bound to serve their lord, just as vassals were.

clue.text: Woman's smart hairstyle trimmed front and back

definitions.note: the apostrophe-s stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: trimming the front and back of these words leaves a run of letters from their middle

explanation.surface: A woman's chic haircut is given a trim at the front and the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, borne by the biblical sister of Mary and Lazarus.
